semantically_equivalent_domains.justification: Adversarial perturbation detection and adversarial detection focus on identifying and detecting adversarial elements in machine learning models, hence they are semantically equivalent.

parent_domains.justification: Adversarial detection encompasses the detection of adversarial perturbations along with other types of adversarial activities, making it a broader category.
Adversarial learning is a broader domain that includes various techniques associated with adversaries, including perturbation detection, making it a parent domain.
Adversarial machine learning is an overarching domain that covers all aspects of adversarial activities in machine learning, including detection of adversarial perturbations.
Although broader, machine learning security includes the security aspects of machine learning, under which adversarial perturbation detection can be categorized.

closest_parent_domain.justification: Adversarial detection is more directly focused on the detection of adversarial actions or perturbations within machine learning models, making it the closest parent domain for adversarial perturbation detection.

child_domains.justification: Adversarial attack detection is a specialization within adversarial perturbation detection, focusing specifically on the detection of adversarial attacks.
This domain is a specific type of adversarial attack detection, which would fall under the broader category of adversarial perturbation detection when specialized for text data.
Adversarial text detection focuses on textual data, so it is a child domain of the broader adversarial perturbation detection area.

closest_child_domain.justification: Adversarial attack detection is the closest child domain as it specifically refers to detecting adversarial attacks, which are often introduced through perturbations.

sibling_domains.justification: Adversarial training and adversarial perturbation detection share the closest parent domain of adversarial detection, making them sibling domains.
Adversarial robustness involves developing resilience to adversarial perturbations, thus is a sibling to adversarial perturbation detection under adversarial detection.
This domain deals with both aspects of adversaries in ML and is related but does not focus solely on detection, making it a sibling.

closest_sibling_domain.justification: Adversarial training is closely aligned with adversarial perturbation detection as both aim to combat adversarial challenges, one through detection and the other through training techniques.

unrelated_domains.justification: Generative adversarial networks focus on generating data and are not directly related to adversarial perturbation detection.
This domain is technical and mathematical in nature, dealing with gradient calculations, and does not pertain to adversarial detection.
While related to robustness, robust generalization is more about the ability of a model to perform well on unseen data, a different focus than adversarial perturbation detection.
